title: Quad-layout pipeline at scan scale: full-resolution crawfish GLB without OOM
description:
Run the `quad_layout` node end to end on one unmodified crawfish scan (~623k vertices / ~936k triangles) and make it finish. The pipeline is tuned around ~15k-vertex inputs (fertility) and the ARCHITECTURE.md constraint is no OOM at 100k-500k vertices. This ticket is explicitly NOT decimation: the user ruled that the quad layout is the compression step and degrading the input is not acceptable, so any stage that cannot scale is improved. Method: profile with `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene quad-layout --profile --property ixdar.model=<scan.glb>` (async-profiler flame graph, read with `python3 -m ixdar_automation_cli.async_profile profile.html --top 30`), attack the top self-time methods and the allocation hot spots (boxing faceIdToActive/edgeIdToActive maps, per-element object allocation in seamless/embedding, Cholesky fill on the seamless system, motorcycle trace storage), and re-verify fertility reproduces the REFACTOR-PLAN-2 baseline unchanged (13853 quads, 284 patches, singularities 44). Record per-stage timings and peak heap as a benchmark. Related solver/decomposer scaling tickets in the PATCH epic: PATCH-12, PATCH-46, PATCH-55, PATCH-103; do not duplicate their fixes, link them.

Note 2026-09-06: after CRAW-12's loader weld the scan arrives with 468,350 vertices and no seam boundaries, so the benchmark's throwaway weld becomes unnecessary and seams no longer register as alignment edges.
definition-of-done: 1. `quad_layout` on IMG_4109.glb reaches a quantized, embedded layout in the quad-layout scene under -Xmx8g without OOM. 2. Per-stage timings (cross field, seamless, motorcycle, quantization, embedding, newton, extraction) and peak heap are recorded in a benchmark test under ixdar-app/test/benchmark/ and in this ticket's changes-made. 3. Fertility baseline from REFACTOR-PLAN-2 reproduces exactly (13853 quads, 284 patches, singularities 44, euler -6). 4. Any stage rewritten keeps its unit tests green and adds none that load meshes into the unit suite. 5. No new System.getProperty knobs; behaviour switches are public fields. 6. Build is checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Run the profiled scene on the scan before changes; save the hot-method table to the ticket. 2. After each fix, re-run and confirm the targeted method's self-time dropped; keep a before/after table. 3. `mvn clean test -pl annotations,ixdar-app` -- the three known-failing quad-layout classes stay the only failures. 4. run-scene screenshot of the crawfish layout with patch fill (P) on for the ticket record.

Replace boxing id->active maps in the hot stage with primitive arrays
Audit per-element allocations in seamless and embedding for reuse fields
Add the crawfish pipeline benchmark with per-stage timing and peak heap
seamless_uv writes its parameterization into the _uv slot (CornerUvField from CRAW-12) on its output geometry; one UV slot per geometry value, ports unchanged for now

Next blocker (2026-09-19): the BCE13 injectivity-constraint loop diverges on the repaired scan (6628218 constraints over 938302 faces; violated 3257 -> 20104 over five rounds, ipIterations=10 converged=false every round, singular pivots in the constraint block at 936612 of 937153, round 1 byte-identical across runs). PATCH-107, the nearest relative, is DONE and did not cover this, so it is CRAW-2's own next step unless split into a PATCH ticket. Check first whether the cross field's Poincare-Hopf violation on the scan (indexSum4=7 against fourChi=-80, about 189 phantom singularities) is the reason no feasible point exists.
unknowns: Whether the Trellis2 scans are 2-manifold and watertight as exported; non-manifold input may need a repair node before cross field (out of scope here -- report it)
Whether the 60s grid-map optimizer budget needs to scale with patch count
Whether alpha_degrees / target_edge_length defaults produce a usable patch count on a 900k-triangle input

ANSWERED, and it is the blocker: the Trellis2 scans are NOT 2-manifold as exported. IMG_4109.glb is unwelded (622652 vertices for 468350 distinct positions, 298169 apparent boundary edges), and even welded it has 125 non-manifold edges, 33 inconsistently oriented edges, 2 degenerate faces, 943 real boundary edges and 14 edge-connected shells. The half-edge build rejects it outright. A repair node (weld by position -> drop non-manifold faces -> pick/keep shells -> report holes) is now on the critical path for CRAW-2, not optional; CRAW-2's benchmark carries a throwaway copy of that repair so the pipeline can be measured at all. Needs its own ticket and a ruling on which shells count as the model.

Whether the fertility layout must stay byte-identical in its INTERMEDIATES, not just its output. Flattening the leftover-constraint rows changed their entry order (a HashMap's iteration order is not insertion order), so the seamless solution moves in its last bits: the recarve working copy goes V=219644 -> 235940 (F=439300 -> 471892, path steps 40050 -> 43536) and grid-optimize worstMove 15.5338 -> 15.5337. Every published baseline number is unchanged (13853 quads, 284 patches, 278 nodes, 568 arcs, singularities 44 indexSum4=-24, euler -6, energy 5.5512e+07 -> 4.0197e+04, 49 iterations, 0/38450 flipped). If bit-identical intermediates are required, SparseConstraintRows has to go and the 4.4M-HashMap path comes back.

NEW BLOCKER, replacing the PARDISO -4 one: the BCE13 injectivity-constraint loop diverges at scan scale. With the seamless system finally factorizing, SeamlessParameterization.runInjectivityConstraintLoop now runs and grows without bound on IMG_4109.glb: round 0 violated=3257 active=0, round 1 violated=8132 active=24138, round 2 violated=10960 active=51542, round 3 violated=15226 active=92964, round 4 violated=20104 active=148590, at 17-25s a round. Every round reports ipIterations=10 factorizations=10 converged=false, so InteriorPointQp is hitting its iteration cap and handing back an infeasible point, and LazyConstraints then adds more constraints than the round removed. At maxConstraintRounds=60 that extrapolates to roughly 3M active constraints and about half an hour, which is why the run was stopped at round 4 rather than left to exhaust a 14GB machine shared with five other worktrees. Each round also logs `[interior-point] singular condensed system (PARDISO ... pivot 936612 of 937153 ...); regularisation fraction raised to 1.000e-10` -- the pivot sits at the very end of the matrix, i.e. in the constraint block, so the constraint Jacobian is rank deficient, not the energy. InjectivityConstraints already skips faces with faceArea <= 0, so it is not the 173 zero-area faces. This is the same family as PATCH-107 (Bolt fails in the injectivity-constraint loop, PARDISO singular at pivot 5678); left to that ticket rather than duplicated here. Until it converges or is deliberately bounded, DoD 1 cannot be reached.

The cross field on the repaired scan violates Poincare-Hopf and nobody has decided whether that matters: `[n-field] singularities=1981 indexSum4=7 fourChi=-80`. The index sum must equal 4*chi for a valid cross field, and chi=-20 for the repaired mesh (7 shells), so indexSum4 should be -80 and is 7. The conversion also warns that the raw field has 1792 singular triangles but the extraction found 1981 vertex singularities, listing hundreds of phantom singularities (vertices carrying an index no raw singular triangle touches). Fertility is clean on the same code path (singularities=44 indexSum4=-24 fourChi=-24), so this is scale or scan specific, not a regression. Unknown whether the motorcycle graph and quantization can produce a sane layout from a field whose indices do not sum to the Euler characteristic, or whether this has to be fixed first; it may also be the reason the injectivity loop cannot find a feasible point.
changes-made: CRAW-2 baseline: quad_layout on IMG_4109.glb never reached a stage -- the scan is not a 2-manifold. Measured on the raw GLB: 622652 V / 936035 F, 298169 boundary edges because the glTF is unwelded (154302 duplicate positions, one vertex per UV-seam corner); welded by exact position it is 468350 V / 1404394 E with 943 boundary edges, 125 non-manifold edges, 33 inconsistently oriented edges and 2 degenerate faces, so HalfEdgeMeshEngine.bulkAllocate throws InvalidMeshTopologyException. Welded it is also 14 edge-connected shells (919762 / 15118 / 214 / 186 / 148 / 128 / 111 / 108 / 38 / 26 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1 faces).

Cut graph: initialCutFromDualSpanningTree seeded its dual Dijkstra from face 0 only, so on any multi-component input every edge outside face 0's component stayed cut. Now a spanning FOREST, one tree per component (CutGraph.growSpanningTree). On the repaired scan this took cut edges 1381924 -> 30624 of 1404337, chart vertices 2770005 -> 497991, raw seamless DOFs 7179266 -> 1017252, leftover constraint rows 4401973 -> 82340, nnz 15446868 -> 285020. Fertility is one component so the forest equals the old tree there.

CrossField/SeamlessUv faceIdToActive and edgeIdToActive were HashMap<Integer,Integer> (936k + 1.4M boxed entries, hashed on every SeamlessUv.u/v/faceCornerUv call). Both are now int[] indexed by element id, built by NDirectionField.activeIndexById.

NDirectionField.angleInFrame was a HashMap<Long,Double> keyed on (vertexId, halfEdge) with one entry per half-edge (5.6M on the scan). A half-edge already names its start vertex, so it is now a double[] indexed by half-edge id, NaN where unset; activeOfVertexId and populate()'s vIdToActive are int[] the same way.

Seamless leftover constraints were built as ArrayList<HashMap<Integer,Double>>, one HashMap per row -- 4.4M of them on the scan, several GB before elimination even started. New SparseConstraintRows holds them in one flat (rowStart, entryDof, entryCoef) triple and LeftoverConstraintEliminator reads that; 12 bytes an entry instead of a few hundred.

HalfEdgeMesh.halfEdgeEndVertex read halfEdgeVertex[halfEdgeNext[he]], which is -1 for a boundary half-edge (no face, so no next). It now reads the twin's start vertex, identical for interior half-edges and defined on the boundary. Without this the cross field dies at NDirectionField.computeVertexFrames on any mesh with a hole.

Per-stage measurement, -Xmx4g, benchmark.CrawfishQuadLayoutBenchmark on IMG_4109.glb welded + repaired to its largest edge-connected shell (V=460289 E=1380199 F=919762): load 0.26s/72MiB, repair 2.22s/598MiB, toHalfEdge 0.58s/1264MiB, cross field 22.3s/3272MiB (1646 singularities; assemble 6.6-7.9s, aligned PCG solve 12.3s). Seamless now reaches the greedy-rounding factorization instead of dying in the leftover reduction; before the fixes the leftover reduction OOM'd at -Xmx4g.

Remaining blocker at seamless: PARDISO phase 12 returns -4 (zero pivot) factorizing the 999796-raw-DOF seamless system in GreedyRounding.run -> DirectSolver.factorizeWithPerm, and CholeskyBackend throws rather than dropping to the next rung of the ladder. Reached with a single edge-connected shell, so it is not the multi-component gauge; suspect rank deficiency from the scan's slivers/handles (repaired shell euler = -148) or a PARDISO limit at this size.

Added ixdar-app/test/benchmark/CrawfishQuadLayoutBenchmark.java (-Dbenchmark.glb, -Dbenchmark.stage): loads the scan, welds it, drops non-manifold faces, keeps the largest edge-connected shell, then runs the pipeline stage by stage logging wall time and peak heap per stage, re-logging the whole table in a finally block so an OOM still leaves the earlier rows. The repair lives in the benchmark on purpose -- it is measurement scaffolding, not the repair node the pipeline needs.

Added the .vscode/launch.json entry 'CRAW-2: Quad Layout (crawfish scan, full resolution)' (ixdar.canvas.IxdarWindow, args quad-layout, -Xmx8g, -Dixdar.model=/home/acw/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb, cwd ${workspaceFolder}/ixdar-app). It currently dies in ArrayMesh.toHalfEdgeMesh with InvalidMeshTopologyException, since the scene has no repair step.

Fertility regression after all five changes (run-scene --scene quad-layout --mesh fertility): singularities 44 indexSum4=-24 fourChi=-24, motorcycle traces=200 arcs=4202 nodes=2145 patches=2051, recarve nodes=278 arcs=568 patches=284, grid-optimize energy 5.5512e+07 -> 4.0197e+04 iterations=49 flipped=0/38450, quads=13853 euler=-6, patch-grids patches=284. Matches the REFACTOR-PLAN-2 baseline. Unit suite: 165 tests, 1 failure, the known DenseMeshFewSplitsTest '9 to 37'.

CORRECTION to the launch-entry note above: the UNMODIFIED scan does load into a HalfEdgeMesh -- the unwelded glTF has no non-manifold edge, only 298169 boundary ones, and InvalidMeshTopologyException appears only after welding. With the halfEdgeEndVertex and spanning-forest fixes the quad-layout scene on -Dixdar.model=/home/acw/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb under -Xmx8g now gets: cross field 86.4s (86 singularities), cut graph 320035 cut edges of 1553137 (interior 21866), chart vertices 658243, leftover rows 343704 (45502 cut + 298202 alignment) over 1318256 raw DOFs, then the same PARDISO phase 12 error -4. Before this ticket it died in NDirectionField.computeVertexFrames at 2s. Note the 298202 alignment edges: unwelded, every texture seam reads as a sharp feature, which is a second reason to weld before the field.

Not done: DoD 1 (no quantized/embedded layout yet -- seamless Cholesky fails), DoD 2 partially (benchmark exists and records load/repair/toHalfEdge/crossField; the later stages have no numbers because the run does not reach them). DoD 3, 4, 5, 6 met. Ticket stays IN_PROGRESS.

ROOT CAUSE of the PARDISO -4, found and fixed: the seamless matrix held NaN, it was never rank deficiency. The tell was that the shift ladder failed at the SAME pivot (10060 of 937141) at every shift from 1.09e-9 up to 1.09 -- a real null space clears under a shift, a NaN row never does. HalfEdgeMeshEngine leaves a zero-area face's normal at (0,0,0) rather than NaN, but NDirectionField.buildFramesAndTransport then did `normal.cross(xAxis, yAxis).normalize()`, and normalizing a zero cross product gives NaN, so faceY was NaN on every zero-area face. SeamlessParameterization's degenerate guard is `Math.abs(twoArea) < 1e-30`, which is false for NaN, so those faces skipped the guard and scattered NaN into faceShapeB/C and from there into the assembled matrix. The repaired IMG_4109.glb has 173 zero-area faces, all of them minted by repair_mesh's hole filling (fixDegenerates runs before fillHoles). Fix: NDirectionField gives a zero-area face an arbitrary finite frame (0,0,1) and counts them; the face's own contributions are zero either way, so a finite mesh is bit-identical. With that one change PARDISO factorizes the 937141-equation seamless system cleanly -- no singular-system line at all, greedy integer rounding completes, and the stage reaches the BCE13 injectivity loop for the first time.

Second real defect on the same path: the seamless gauge was anchored once for the whole mesh. AssemblyPlanBuilder.finish walked the chart vertices, added NULLSPACE_ANCHOR_WEIGHT to the first primary one and `break`ed. The energy reads only UV gradients, so every edge-connected surface component has its own free translation; with one anchor, a k-component mesh leaves 2(k-1) exact null directions. This never showed before because the cut graph seeded from face 0 only, so multi-component input never got this far. repair_mesh keeps 7 shells of IMG_4109.glb (largest 919950 faces, the rest 100..15118), so 12 null directions. Fix: CutGraph labels each active face with its edge-connected surface component during the dual spanning forest (surfaceComponentOfFace / surfaceComponentCount, logged on the cut-graph line), and AssemblyPlanBuilder.anchorGaugePerSurfaceComponent anchors one primary chart vertex per component. On a single-component mesh it picks the same chart vertex the old `break` picked, so fertility is untouched.

Deliberate ladder fallback (ticket todo 4), which is also what identified the NaN: CholeskyBackend.factor retried a singular native factorization on exactly one diagonal shift (1e-10 of the largest free diagonal) and then dropped to EJML, which at ~937k DOFs is not a fallback -- the unshifted EJML rung failed in seconds and the shifted one ran without end. It now escalates the shift over SINGULAR_SHIFT_RUNGS=4 rungs, each SINGULAR_SHIFT_ESCALATION=1e3 times the last (1.09e-9 .. 1.09e0 here), stamping the shift that succeeded on the matrix so the diagnosis reads the right one, and only then falls through. A gauge null space clears on the first rung. The rung that mattered for the diagnosis was the LAST one: failing at the same pivot 10060 under a shift of 1.09 is impossible for a rank deficiency, which is what pointed at NaN rather than rank. Healthy factorizations never enter this path, so nothing that factorizes today changes.

CrawfishQuadLayoutBenchmark's throwaway repairToOneManifoldShell is gone; it now calls MeshRepair (CRAW-26) with RepairMeshNode's own defaults (max_hole_edges 4096, min_shell_faces 100, weld_epsilon 0) and takes the half-edge mesh straight off repair.output, so the separate toHalfEdge row disappears with it. That deleted about 200 lines of weld/drop/union-find scaffolding from the test tree. The load and repair rows reproduce CRAW-26's reference within noise: V 468350->469131, F 936035->938302, 0 boundary edges, E 1407453 (CRAW-26 reported 469131 V / 1407453 E / 938302 F); repair 2.21-2.36s against the reference 2.6-3.0s, load 0.45-0.55s. The 4.98s first reading was a cold JVM with five sibling worktrees compiling; the steady-state reading is inside the 1% the todo asked for on the counts and a little faster on the clock. Report line: welded=0 oriented=0 mobius=33 nonManifoldEdges=158 splitVertices=396 degenerate=4 shells=74 dropped=67 holes=74 filled=74 open=0 oversized=0 unfillable=0.

The quad-layout scene could not load the scan at all, which is the first half of DoD 1. ModelScene.loadModel built the half-edge mesh straight from the file, and since CRAW-12's loader weld the scan arrives welded with 125-158 non-manifold edges, so HalfEdgeMeshEngine rejected it and the launch entry died before any stage ran. ModelScene.loadModel now catches InvalidMeshTopologyException and re-reads the file through MeshRepair with RepairMeshNode's defaults, logging the model path, what the direct build objected to, and the repair's summary line. A mesh the direct build accepts never touches this path, so every existing scene and model is byte-identical (fertility's run logs no `not 2-manifold` line). This is the recovery path, not a switch: no new field and no property, and the scene and the benchmark now run the same repair with the same parameters, so their numbers are comparable.

Per-stage wall time and peak heap on IMG_4109.glb, -Xmx8g, repair_mesh defaults, alpha 15 deg, five sibling worktrees building on the same 14GB machine (so the clock is pessimistic, the heap is not): load 0.55s / 211MiB; repair 2.21s / 979MiB (V 468350->469131, E 1407453, F 938302, 0 boundary edges); crossField 39.76s / 4168MiB, of which assemble 17.78s, hopf solve 0.53s, aligned solve 18.63s, face frames 0.06s with 173 zero-area faces framed arbitrarily. Seamless now gets through the parts that used to kill it: cut graph 31105 cut edges of 1407453 (all interior, 0 boundary since repair_mesh fills every hole), 500263 chart vertices (480373 primary) of 2814906 corners, 7 surface components; leftover reduction 85952 rows (84640 cut, 1312 alignment), nnz 299060 over 1022956 raw DOFs; greedy integer rounding factorizes 937141 equations with no singular-system line at all. The stage does not finish: it is the BCE13 injectivity loop that now runs away (see the new unknown), so the seamless row and everything after it have no number yet. For contrast, the previous record on this ticket died in the leftover reduction at -Xmx4g and then at PARDISO phase 12 error -4.

Verification of this session's five changes. Fertility (run-scene --scene quad-layout --mesh fertility) reproduces every published output number exactly: singularities=44 indexSum4=-24 fourChi=-24, motorcycle traces=200 arcs=4202 nodes=2145 patches=2051, recarve nodes=278 arcs=568 patches=284, quads=13853 euler=-6, patch-grids patches=284, grid-optimize flipped=0/38450. Stronger than a match, the changes are provably inert there: the run logs `0 zero-area faces framed arbitrarily` (so the frame fix never fires), `surface components 1` (so the per-component anchor picks the same single chart vertex the old `break` picked), and zero occurrences of `singular system` or `not 2-manifold` (so neither the shift ladder nor the scene's repair fallback runs). Two intermediates moved against the older record in this ticket -- grid-optimize energy 5.5509e+07 -> 4.0199e+04 in 40 iterations against 5.5512e+07 -> 4.0197e+04 in 49, and the recarve working copy V=234654 path steps 43421 against V=235940 / 43536 -- but that drift is master's 24 commits, not this diff, which cannot reach fertility at all by the three log facts above. APPLIED ASSUMPTION, reversible by the user: the ruling taken for this session is that the published OUTPUT numbers must match exactly while intermediates may differ in their last bits, so SparseConstraintRows stays. If the user reverses it and requires bit-identical intermediates, SparseConstraintRows has to go and the 4.4M-HashMap path comes back. Unit suite: 293 tests, 1 failure, HeapSamplerTest.peakRisesWithALiveAllocationAndResetsWithTheWindow, which passes 3/3 when run alone -- a GC-timing flake under the suite's own memory pressure, unrelated to this diff (it measures MemoryPoolMXBean peaks). Build is checkstyle-green and no System.getProperty knob was added.

Second measured run, to patchSurfaces, confirming the stage table and pinning the new blocker: load 1.17s/211MiB, repair 2.37s/975MiB, crossField 43.62s/4434MiB, seamless dof system 1.689s, and -- the headline -- greedy integer rounding 13.155s, the step that returned PARDISO phase 12 error -4 for the whole life of this ticket. Then `[injectivity] constraints=6628218 over 938302 faces`, 7.06 candidate injectivity constraints per face, and the lazy loop diverges from there: round 0 violated=3257 active=0, round 1 violated=8132 active=24138, byte-for-byte the same numbers as the previous run, so the divergence is deterministic rather than load noise. Stopped at round 1 of 60 rather than burn half an hour of a 14GB machine shared with five other worktrees on a loop already known to grow.

DoD status after this session. DoD 1 NOT met: the scan now loads into the quad-layout scene (ModelScene repairs on rejection) and the seamless system factorizes in 13s, but the BCE13 injectivity loop does not terminate usefully, so there is no quantized, embedded layout yet -- the blocker moved from PARDISO phase 12 error -4 to the injectivity loop, which is the new unknown and PATCH-107's family. DoD 2 PARTIAL: the benchmark records load / repair / crossField with wall time and peak heap, in the file and in changes-made above; seamless and everything after it still have no row because the run does not get through them. DoD 3 MET, and proved inert rather than merely equal (see the verification entry). DoD 4 MET: 293 tests, the one failure is the GC-timing flake HeapSamplerTest, which passes 3/3 alone; no test loads a mesh. DoD 5 MET: no System.getProperty added; the two new behaviours are an error-recovery path (ModelScene) and constants on CholeskyBackend. DoD 6 MET: mvn -o compile clean, checkstyle included. Ticket stays IN_PROGRESS. The next agent should start at the injectivity loop, not at the solver: the seamless Cholesky question this ticket carried for weeks is answered and closed.
